sections.title: New Approaches to an Architecture of Health
sections.description: Health care is taking on a new role in our society - with a refocusing from episodic care for those who are ill or symptomatic to providing life-long care geared towards maintaining wellness. These changes are evident across numerous areas of design, from wearable technologies that track and analyze, to large scale building initiatives that aim to create healthier environments and improve lives through strategic planning initiatives. A concrete, physical representation of this paradigm shift can be found within the hospital building itself and in the new manner in which hospitals are looking to serve their patients and care for their clinicians. Simultaneously both public and private spaces, hospitals are complex systems in which sickness, health, hospitality, technology, emergency, and community share space and compete for resource. In order to frame our present day understanding of the role of architecture (and design) in fostering health for individuals and within communities, this seminar will begin with an exploration of the historical and contemporary perspectives on the role of the architect and built environment on health. (Parallels between design and our ever-changing understanding of the biological, social, and environmental causes of sickness and disease will also be explored.) During this conversation, students will read articles and study recently constructed projects in order to examine the ways in which the architects approached these topics through built form. Following from this foundation, students will craft arguments for a new approach to the individual, the community, health, and architecture through a written response and architecturally designed scenario that argues for their perspective on how architecture can and should shape the health of those who inhabit it. Throughout the course, students will engage in weekly readings (and discussions) of critical texts exploring ideas around the role and impact of architecture on health. Various content experts will be included in the course to provide additional insights into key areas of theory and practice in order to lend additional perspectives and ground the conversation.

sections.title: Architecture and Design for Health
sections.description: Architecture and Design for Health: Creating places, products, and experiences for people: In this course, you will examine how design and architecture shape everyday environments by grounding inquiry in our shared human experience of the built world. Emphasizing design as an active and non-neutral practice, you will explore how spaces, objects, and systems impact bodies, influence behavior, and shape well-being. The course draws on readings, conversation, collaborative activities, and guest speakers to engage contemporary perspectives, with an emphasis on learning through application rather than discussion alone. You will apply these ideas through in-class exercises and more developed design investigations that explore how design choices shape everyday life. You will also have the opportunity to develop project work in ways that align with your learning interests and professional goals. This course foregrounds interdisciplinary exchange. Past students have come from Architecture, Integrated Product Design, Landscape Architecture, Business, Nursing, and more. Students from a wide range of disciplines are encouraged to enroll.
